*******************
EMode Documentation
*******************

EMode is a software product by EMode Photonix, offering a solution for photonics simulation and device design.

.. card:: **Installation**
   :link: installation
   :link-alt: Installation
   :link-type: doc
   :width: 75%
   :margin: 3

   Step-by-step instructions for installing and configuring EMode.

.. card:: **Interface**
   :link: interface
   :link-alt: Interface
   :link-type: doc
   :width: 75%
   :margin: 3

   Learn how to setup Python to interact with EMode.

.. card:: **EMode Guide**
   :link: emodeguide
   :link-alt: EMode Guide
   :link-type: doc
   :width: 75%
   :margin: 3

   Detailed documentation for all EMode functions.

.. card:: **Examples**
   :link: examples
   :link-alt: Examples
   :link-type: doc
   :width: 75%
   :margin: 3

   A collection of examples and common simulation setups.


Installation
============

1. Get an EMode License
-----------------------

- `Create an EMode account <https://emodephotonix.com/register/>`_, and verify your account via the confirmation email.
- Purchase a subscription license through the `EMode store <https://emodephotonix.com/get-emode/>`_. This is required, even for a free EMode\ :sup:`2D`\  license.

2. Set Up the Python Interface
------------------------------

Follow the :ref:`Python Interface <python-interface>` instructions to install Python and the ``emodeconnection`` package.

3. Download and Install EMode
-----------------------------

**System requirements:** **Windows** 10+, **Linux** Ubuntu 22.04+ (x86-64), **macOS** 13 Ventura+

There are two installation methods:

.. tab-set::

    .. tab-item:: emode-install

        The ``emode-install`` command-line tool is included with the ``emodeconnection``
        Python package. It handles downloading, installing, and updating EMode.
        After installing ``emodeconnection`` via pip, you can run the installer.
        You will be prompted to accept the
        `EMode EULA <https://emodephotonix.com/legal/eula.pdf>`_ and log in
        with your EMode account credentials. For additional options, see the
        :ref:`EMode Install <emode-install>` instructions or run ``emode-install --help``.

        .. code-block:: bash

            emode-install

    .. tab-item:: Manual install

        #. Log in to your `EMode account <https://emodephotonix.com/my-account/>`_.
        #. Select your operating system and version from the dropdown menus.
        #. Accept the EMode End User License Agreement.
        #. Click ``Download EMode`` to download the file for your platform.

        **Windows**

        Unzip the downloaded ``.zip`` file and double-click the installer
        (``.exe``). Follow the on-screen prompts to complete installation.
        EMode will be added to your PATH automatically.

        **macOS**

        Double-click the downloaded ``.pkg`` file and follow the installer
        prompts. Administrator access may be required. EMode will be installed
        to ``/usr/local/bin/emode``.

        **Linux**

        Unzip the downloaded ``.zip`` file and run the ``install.sh`` script:

        .. code-block:: bash

            unzip EMode-VERSION-Linux.zip
            sh install.sh

**macOS Apple silicon:** EMode runs via Rosetta 2 and you may be prompted to install it on the first run.

4. Run an EMode Example Script
------------------------------

- Run the `Basic: SOI <examples/SOI.html>`_ example in Python to verify your installation.
- A login window will open when EMode is first initialized. To subsequently access this window, see :ref:`EMode Login <PythonEModeLogin>`.

If you have any issues, please contact our `support team <https://emodephotonix.com/contact/>`_.

.. hlist::
   :columns: 2

   * `Release notes <installation/release-notes.html>`_
   * `Troubleshooting <installation/troubleshooting.html>`_


.. _python-interface:

Python Interface
================

To control EMode directly from a Python script, we supply a Python package called ``emodeconnection``. This has been tested with Python 3.10 or higher, including the Anaconda distribution, iPython terminals, and numerous IDEs.

The source code can be viewed here: `emodeconnection <https://github.com/emode-photonix/emodeconnection>`_

For more information about Python, see these links:

.. hlist::
   :columns: 3

   - `Download Python <https://www.python.org/downloads/>`_
   - `Python Documentation <https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/>`_
   - `Python Tutorial <https://www.pythontutorial.net/>`_

.. _SetupPython:

Setup
-----

Install the ``emodeconnection`` Python package from the command line.

.. code-block::

   pip install emodeconnection

Update to the latest version with:

.. code-block::

   pip install -U emodeconnection

Alternatively, the ``uv`` package manager may be used in place of ``pip``.

.. _emode-install:

Install EMode
-------------

The ``emode-install`` command-line tool is included with the ``emodeconnection``
Python package. It handles downloading, installing, and updating EMode.
After installing ``emodeconnection`` via pip, you can run the installer.
You will be prompted to accept the
`EMode EULA <https://emodephotonix.com/legal/eula.pdf>`_ and log in
with your EMode account credentials. For additional complete options,
run ``emode-install --help``.

.. code-block:: bash

    emode-install

Additional options:

.. code-block:: bash

    emode-install                            # Install latest version
    emode-install --help                     # Show all options
    emode-install --list-versions            # Show available versions
    emode-install --update                   # Update to the latest version
    emode-install --update --version 0.2.5   # Switch to a specific version
    emode-install --version 0.2.5            # Install a specific version
    emode-install --install-dir /opt/bin     # Custom install directory
    emode-install --uninstall                # Remove EMode
    emode-install --uninstall --install-dir /opt/bin  # Remove from custom location

For automated or headless installs, set these environment variables
to skip interactive prompts:

+-------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| Variable                | Description                                     |
+=========================+=================================================+
| `EMODE_EULA_ACCEPTED=1` | Accept the EULA non-interactively (CI/headless) |
+-------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| `EMODE_EMAIL`           | Pre-fill login email                            |
+-------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| `EMODE_PASSWORD`        | Pre-fill password (use with caution)            |
+-------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| `EMODE_INTERACTIVE=1`   | Use interactive installer GUI                   |
+-------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| `UNINSTALL_EMODE=y`     | Accept the uninstallation non-interactively     |
+-------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+

.. _PythonEModeLogin:

EMode Login
-----------

Open the EMode Login GUI from a Python session to login to your EMode Photonix account and view your license subscriptions and active sessions. *Alternatively*, you can run ``emode`` from the command line to launch the login GUI. Once logged in, click the exit button to close the GUI and save the login credentials.

.. code-block::

   import emodeconnection as emc
   emc.EModeLogin()

To clear active sessions, select an option from the dropdown in the *Active Sessions* header row and click *Clear*. This terminates the selected sessions without consuming a license seat and refreshes the session table. The options are 'none' (default), 'all' (all non-roaming sessions), 'mine' (only sessions launched by the current user), 'others' (sessions owned by the current user but launched by other shared users), 'latest' (the latest non-roaming session), and 'oldest' (the oldest non-roaming session).

Command-line login
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Run ``emode login`` from the command line for an interactive text version of the login GUI. It validates any stored credentials against the license server and prompts for your email and password if they are missing or invalid; credentials are only saved after successful validation. It then displays your subscriptions and active sessions, prompts for a session-clearing option (the same options as the GUI dropdown), and asks whether to log out on this computer.

.. code-block:: bash

   emode login

To enter credentials without contacting the license server, run ``emode login --write``. This prompts for your email and password and writes them directly, without validation or session display. Use this as a basic fallback interface when the license server is unreachable.

The EMode class
---------------

.. class:: EMode(simulation_name = 'emode', license_type = 'default', clear = 'none', save_path = '.', verbose = False, roaming = False, open_existing = False, new_name = False, priority = 'pN', emode_cmd = None, force_open = False, save = True)

    Opens the EMode software and initializes a local simulation file. The user's account must have an active license available to successfully run EMode. If the user has not previously logged in, this will prompt for a username and password. To reset the user profile, run ``emode login --write`` from the command line.

    An existing file can be opened for further analysis by specifying the input argument ``open_existing = True``. This opened file can be copied to a new file name by specifying the input argument ``new_name = 'new_filename'``.

    .. note::
        All `EMode functions <emodeguide.html>`_ are accessible as methods of this class instance using keyword arguments for each function input parameter.

    :param str simulation_name: Name of the simulation file. The extension '.eph' will be added to this name. Default: 'emode'.
    :param str license_type: The requested license type, either '2d', '3d', or 'default'. When running with 'default' license type, a '3d' license will be initialized if it is available, otherwise a '2d' license will be initialized if it is available. The '2d' or '3d' options will only request that specific license type if it is available. Default: 'default'.
    :param str clear: Indicate whether to clear existing EMode sessions from this computer. Accepts 'all' (all non-roaming sessions), 'mine' (only sessions launched by the current user), 'others' (sessions owned by the current user but launched by other shared users), 'latest'/'oldest' (the latest/oldest non-roaming session), and 'none'. Clearing can be used when a session crashes to free up a license seat, but it will terminate the associated session. Default: 'none'.
    :param save_path: Name of the path where the simulation file will be created and saved. Default: '.'.
    :type save_path: str or ~pathlib.Path
    :param bool verbose: Whether to run EMode in verbose mode for debugging. Default: False.
    :param bool roaming: Set the license manager to roaming mode. Normal mode (roaming = False) re-checks the license connection every 2 minutes, allowing licenses to reset after 10 minutes if the internet connection fails. Roaming mode (roaming = True) can be used to extend the license re-check to 24 hours to support long simulations without continuously re-checking the license. When ending a session normally on roaming, the license is checked-in. However, when a session crashes, the license will remain checked-out until 24 hours after the start. Use the ``clear`` parameter or the :ref:`EMode Login <PythonEModeLogin>` session clearing to terminate ghost license check-outs. Default: False.
    :param bool open_existing: Whether to open an existing file or to start a new simulation. Default: False.
    :param new_name: New name of opened existing file so the original file does not get modified. If False the original name is used. The extension '.eph' will be added to this name. Default: False.
    :type new_name: bool or str
    :param str priority: Set the CPU process priority. 'pH': High; 'pAN': Above normal; 'pN': Normal; 'pBN': Below normal; 'pI': Idle. Default: 'pN' (Normal).
    :param list[str] emode_cmd: Set the EMode executable command. For standard installations, this can be ignored. Only use this if the EMode executable has been moved to a custom location, or if multiple versions are installed in different locations.
    :param bool force_open: If a simulation file with this name is already open elsewhere, open it anyway instead of auto-renaming. Default: False.
    :param bool save: Whether to save the simulation file when the session ends. Set to False to run without writing to disk. Default: True.

Functions
---------

The ``emodeconnection`` package provides access to EMode Login GUI and to the EMode simulation files without using an active EMode license. This is helpful for analyzing simulation data without checking out an EMode license or for sharing the EMode simulation results with a collaborator who does not have an EMode license.

.. function:: EModeLogin()

    Opens the EMode Login GUI to input your EMode Photonix account credentials, view active license subscriptions, and view or clear active sessions (see :ref:`EMode Login <PythonEModeLogin>`). Once logged in, click the exit button to close the GUI and save the login credentials.

.. function:: open_file(sim = 'emode', simulation_name = None)

    Opens an EMode simulation file with the extension '.eph' or '.mat' and returns a dictionary with the file contents.

    :param str sim: Name of the simulation file. The '.eph' or '.mat' extension is optional to include with the name. Default: 'emode'.
    :param str simulation_name: Alternative to ``sim``; if given, overrides it. Default: None.
    :return: Dictionary with all keys and data from the specified EMode simulation file.
    :rtype: dict

.. function:: get(variable, sim = 'emode', simulation_name = None)

    Returns the contents of a specified variable from an EMode simulation file with the extension '.eph' or '.mat'.

    :param str variable: Name of the variable to return from EMode.
    :param str sim: Name of the simulation file. The '.eph' or '.mat' extension is optional to include with the name. Default: 'emode'.
    :param str simulation_name: Alternative to ``sim``; if given, overrides it. Default: None.
    :return: Requested item from EMode.
    :rtype: int, float, str, or array-like

.. function:: inspect(sim = 'emode', simulation_name = None)

    Get the names of all variables from EMode simulation file with the extension '.eph' or '.mat'.

    :param str sim: Name of the simulation file. The '.eph' or '.mat' extension is optional to include with the name. Default: 'emode'.
    :param str simulation_name: Alternative to ``sim``; if given, overrides it. Default: None.
    :return: List of names of all variables available in the EMode simulation file. Any of these variables can be extracted to the user with the `get()` function.
    :rtype: list

Constants
---------

The ``emodeconnection.constants`` module contains the following constants.

.. py:attribute:: c

   The speed of light in vacuum in m/s.

.. py:attribute:: eps_0

   The vacuum permittivity in F/m.

.. py:attribute:: mu_0

   The vacuum permeability in H/m.

.. py:attribute:: eta

   The impedance of free space in Ohms.

.. py:attribute:: e

   The elementary charge in C.

.. py:attribute:: hbar

   The reduced Planck constant in J·s.

Types
-----

Four types are available as classes of the emodeconnection package to specify material properties, field data, and grid data.

.. py:class:: MaterialProperties

   A container for linear and non-linear electromagnetic material parameters. At least one of `n` or `eps` **must** be supplied in any valid instance.

   :param n: Scalar or tensor refractive index. Accepts *None* (unspecified), a float, a list of 3 floats (for x,y,z), or a 3 x 3 list of list of floats for an anisotropic material.
   :type n: ~typing.Optional[float | list[float] | list[list[float]]]

   :param eps: Relative permittivity tensor εᵣ. Accepts *None* (unspecified), a float, a list of 3 floats (for x,y,z), or a 3 x 3 list of list of floats for a fully anisotropic material.
   :type eps: ~typing.Optional[float | list[float] | list[list[float]]]

   :param mu: Relative permeability tensor μᵣ. Same shape conventions as `eps`. Default: *None* (μᵣ = 1).
   :type mu: ~typing.Optional[float | list[float] | list[list[float]]]

   :param d: Second-order nonlinear susceptibility *d*. Expected shape is 3x6. Use *None* when the material is linear. Default: *None*.
   :type d: ~typing.Optional[~DTensorType]

----

.. py:class:: MaterialSpec

   A container that defines the adjustable properties of a material being used. All properties default to the materials
   defaults (typically 0).

   :param material: Either a *str* pointing to a material in the Material Database, or a MaterialProperties object. Required.
   :type material: ~typing.Union[str, ~MaterialProperties]

   :param theta: The angle of rotation around *y* for the material in radians.
   :type theta: ~typing.Optional[float]

   :param phi: The angle of rotation around *z* for the material in radians. This is applied *after* the theta rotation.
   :type phi: ~typing.Optional[float]

   :param x: The mole fraction for ternary materials such as AlGaAs and InGaAs. This is ignored in materials without this parameter.  Must be between 0 and 1.
   :type x: ~typing.Optional[float]

   :param loss: The absorption loss of the material in dB/m.
   :type loss: ~typing.Optional[float]

----

.. py:class:: Field

   A container for field data.

   :param field: An array of all of the fields, including all modes with shape [N_fields, N_modes, Nx, Ny].
   :type field: array-like

   :param field_names: A list of the field names, corresponding to the fields in the ``field`` array.
   :type field_names: list[str]

   :param num_modes: The number of modes.
   :type num_modes: int

   :param grid: A grid object associated with the fields.
   :type grid: Grid

----

.. py:class:: Grid

   A container that defines the simulation grid.

   :param x: Array of the x grid center points of the mesh.
   :type x: array-like

   :param y: Array of the y grid center points of the mesh.
   :type y: array-like

   :param is_pml: Whether the grid includes a PML region.
   :type is_pml: bool

   :param is_expanded: Whether the grid includes an expansion region.
   :type is_expanded: bool

   :param is_bc: True if the boundary condition is '00', False for other boundary conditions.
   :type is_bc: bool

----

.. py:class:: SMatrix

   A dense, port-structured scattering matrix returned by EME results (e.g. from ``EME()`` or ``get(key='S_matrix')``). Ports are indexed 0 to ``num_ports - 1``; port *i* spans a contiguous range of modes whose count is ``port_sizes[i]``. When ``port_names``/``wavelengths`` are available, ports can also be addressed by name instead of by index.

   :param port_sizes: number of modes in each port.
   :type port_sizes: tuple[int, ...]

   :param data: the complex scattering matrix, with shape ``(total_modes, total_modes)``.
   :type data: ~numpy.ndarray

   :param port_names: name of each port, parallel to ``port_sizes``. Default: None.
   :type port_names: tuple[str, ...] or None

   :param wavelengths: wavelength of each port, parallel to ``port_sizes``. Default: None.
   :type wavelengths: tuple[float, ...] or None

   ``SMatrix`` also provides convenience methods: ``transmission(from_port, to_port)``, ``reflection(port)``, ``insertion_loss_dB(from_port, to_port, mode)``, ``unitarity_error()``, and ``plot(kind)``.

Geometry
--------

The ``emodeconnection.geometry`` module provides classes for defining waveguide centerline paths, used primarily for EME GDS sections.

.. py:class:: Pose(w=0, z=0, x=0, y=0, azimuth=0)

   Position and orientation of a curve's local frame within the section frame.

   :param float w: Lateral offset.
   :param float z: Axial position.
   :param float x: x position.
   :param float y: y position.
   :param float azimuth: Orientation angle in radians.

----

.. py:class:: Line(length)

   Straight segment along the local +z axis.

   :param float length: Length of the segment (must be positive).

----

.. py:class:: Arc(radius, sweep_angle)

   Circular arc segment.

   :param float radius: Bend radius (signed; sign determines bend direction).
   :param float sweep_angle: Subtended angle in radians (signed).

----

.. py:class:: BSpline(knots, coefficients, degree=3)

   B-spline curve segment.

   :param list knots: Knot vector. Must satisfy ``len(knots) == len(coefficients) + degree + 1``.
   :param list coefficients: Control points as a list of ``[x, z]`` pairs.
   :param int degree: Spline degree. Default: 3.

----

.. py:class:: Path(segments)

   A composed waveguide centerline built from one or more curve segments.

   :param tuple segments: Tuple of :py:class:`Line`, :py:class:`Arc`, or :py:class:`BSpline` objects. The total path length is the sum of all segment lengths.

----

.. py:data:: Curve

   Type alias for ``Union[Line, Arc, BSpline]``.

.. _ports:

Ports
-----

The ``emodeconnection.port`` module provides classes for defining named ports on EME sections. Every EME section function accepts a ``ports`` argument (see :doc:`EME </emodeguide/eme>`) that replaces the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-``side`` basis: a supplied port replaces every existing port on that side, and multiple ports may share a side. Ports are addressed globally as ``"<section_name>.<port_name>"`` for explicit wiring with :data:`connect_ports`.

**Connecting two ports pins their coordinate systems together.** The two ports' origins, which are the horizontal center and bottom edge of each port's cross-section, are made to coincide, so a section is positioned by the connection rather than by absolute coordinates. Because the origin is the *bottom* edge in y, two profiles of different heights stay aligned at their substrate rather than at their vertical centers. Use ``offset`` below to displace a section off that shared origin.

.. py:class:: Port(name, window=None, side, offset=(0.0, 0.0))

   A named port on a section.

   A ``Port`` carries two offsets that mean different things: ``window.offset`` says *which part of this section's cross-section the port exposes*, while ``offset`` says *where this section sits* relative to what the port connects to. In short, ``window`` answers "which part of me?" and ``offset`` answers "where am I?". A window never moves a section, and an offset never crops one.

   :param str name: Port name, unique within its section.
   :param window: A rectangular sub-region of the port's full cross-section to isolate, positioned within *this section's own* cross-section. Must overlap the section's profile. When set on a port that is not connected to anything (an unclaimed, external boundary port), the port's mode is solved independently on just this window instead of the section's full cross-section. This is the physically correct choice for exciting or measuring a single waveguide within a wider multi-waveguide cross-section (e.g. one arm of a directional coupler), rather than the coupled full-cross-section supermode. Default: None (the port sees the section's entire cross-section).
   :type window: Bounds or None
   :param str side: Which end of the section this port is declared on, either 'left' or 'right'.
   :param offset: [nm] transverse displacement of this section's cross-section relative to the port it connects to: ``offset=(1300, 0)`` places this section's content 1300 nm in +x from the connection's shared origin. Default: (0, 0). Typically you annotate whichever side is off-axis, e.g. giving a coupler's input port ``offset`` so a centered adapter waveguide lines up with it, rather than offsetting the adapter. The legacy per-section ``offset=`` argument (see :doc:`EME </emodeguide/eme>`) is this same displacement applied to every port at once; setting both on one section raises an :class:`ArgumentError`.
   :type offset: tuple[float, float]

----

.. py:class:: Bounds(window_width, window_height, offset=(0.0, 0.0))

   A rectangular sub-window of a port's full cross-section, used as :class:`Port`'s ``window``.

   :param float window_width: Width of the window, in the cross-section's x-direction.
   :param float window_height: Height of the window, in the cross-section's y-direction.
   :param offset: Position of the window within the port's full cross-section: the x-coordinate of the window's horizontal center, and the y-coordinate of the window's bottom edge. Note the asymmetry: the second entry is the window's **bottom**, not its center, matching the cross-section's own y-axis which starts at 0 at the bottom of the profile. A full-height window therefore wants ``y=0``, not ``-window_height/2``. The window must overlap the section's profile.
   :type offset: tuple[float, float]

Exceptions
----------

The ``emodeconnection.types`` module also contains the following exception classes. All errors in EMode are raised and passed back to the user as one of these errors.

.. py:class:: EModeError(msg='', *args, **kwargs)

   Base class for all EMode exceptions.

   :param str msg: Human-readable explanation. Default: ''.

----

.. py:class:: ArgumentError(msg, function, argument)

   Invalid value passed to *function*.

   :param str msg: Human-readable explanation.
   :param function: Function name, or None.
   :type function: str or None
   :param argument: Name of the offending argument, or None.
   :type argument: str or None

----

.. py:class:: EPHKeyError(msg, filename, key)

   Missing dataset or attribute *key* in the given EPH file.

   :param str msg: Details of the failure.
   :param str filename: Path to the EPH file.
   :param str key: Absent key.

----

.. py:class:: FileError(msg, filename)

   Generic file-system or I/O problem.

   :param str msg: Description of the error.
   :param str filename: File path involved.

----

.. py:class:: LicenseError(msg, license_type)

   Operation not permitted under *license_type*.

   :param str msg: Explanation of the denial.
   :param LicenseType license_type: Active or required licence class.

----

.. py:class:: ShapeError(msg, shape_name)

   Unexpected tensor or geometry shape.

   :param str msg: Explanation of the mismatch.
   :param str shape_name: Symbolic name of the offending shape.

----

.. py:class:: NameError(msg, type, name)

   Forbidden *name* within the given *type* category.

   :param str msg: Reason for the failure.
   :param str type: Category being searched (e.g. ``"section"`` or ``"label"``).
   :param str name: Forbidden identifier.

----

.. py:class:: NotImplementedError(msg)

   Feature is recognised but not yet implemented.

   :param str msg: Description of the missing capability.

--------

Features
--------

.. hlist::
   :columns: 3

   * Finite difference method
   * Scattering loss
   * Bend modes
   * Symmetries
   * Perfectly matched layers
   * Sub-pixel averaging
   * General anisotropy
   * Magnetic materials
   * Non-uniform meshing
   * Eigenmode expansion (EME)
   * Multi-physics (thermal, electrostatic)
   * Second-order nonlinear optics

Finite difference method
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

The finite difference method (FDM) is used to solve the waveguide eigenmodes. The electric and magnetics fields are solved in a Yee grid, and they are subsequently interpolated to common grid points. Features are added to support subpixel averaging, bend modes, anisotropic materials, non-uniform meshing, and mode symmetries.

    Z. Zhu and T. G. Brown, ''Full-vectorial finite-difference analysis of microstructured optical fibers,'' Opt. Express **10**, 853 (2002).

Boundary conditions
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Symmetric or anti-symmetric boundary conditions can be applied to the south and west sides of the simulation window with the setting parameter ``boundary_condition``. By explicitly setting the symmetry with an 'S' (symmetric) or 'A' (anti-symmetric), the refractive index profile is forced to be symmetric in the specified vertical or horizontal direction. Another option is to set the boundary condition to 'TE' or 'TM' and the solver will decide if vertical, horizontal, or both symmetries exist in the specified refractive index profile. These options will choose the appropriate 'S' or 'A' boundaries to solve the fundamental TE or TM mode with the maximum available symmetry.

Meshing
^^^^^^^

Shapes define the refractive index profile of the waveguide and a meshing algorithm using contour-path effective permittivities is implemented. On the Yee grid, the permittivity and permeability arrays are unique for each x, y, and z direction. The plot of the refractive index shows the exact shapes that are defined, and the actual permittivity and permeability arrays are available using the ``get`` method. Calculated fields correspond to the center points of the meshed grid (``x`` and ``y``).

    A. Mohammadi, H. Nadgaran, and M. Agio, ''Contour-path effective permittivities for the two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain method,'' Opt. Express **13**, 10367 (2005).

Non-uniform mesh
""""""""""""""""

A non-uniform mesh can be specified to increase the grid spacing in the perimeter area of the simulation window. This is helpful to reduce the simulation time when using a fine grid mesh. The primary simulation window is defined by the ``window_width``, ``window_height``, ``x_resolution``, and ``y_resolution`` parameters. To add a non-uniform grid, the parameters ``expansion_size`` and ``expansion_resolution`` must be defined. Expanded regions taper the resolution from the primary window to a maximum value of the ``expansion_resolution``. However, the tapering is terminated if the ``expansion_size`` is reached before the resolution has reached the ``expansion_resolution`` value. Unique values for the ``expansion_size`` can be defined for each edge of the simulation window. The user must investigate convergence of the effective index and loss values by varying the window size, expanded area size, and grid resolutions.

Citing EMode
^^^^^^^^^^^^

If you use EMode for design or analysis in a publication, please use the following citation.

    EMode [Software] from EMode Photonix. Available at `emodephotonix.com <https://www.emodephotonix.com>`_.



File management
---------------

Simulation data are stored in an EMode Photonix file with the extension '.eph'. This file is created when a simulation is initialized, and existing simulation files can be opened by EMode for further analysis.

.. data:: init

    Create a simulation instance with an associated '.eph' file to run the simulation and store data. This function is automatically called when the emodeconnection class is initialized.

    :param str save_path: path to save the simulation file relative to the current working directory, default: '.'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: open

    Open an existing simulation '.eph' file. This can be used to retrieve previous simulation data or to run a simulation based on a template.

    :param str save_path: path to open the simulation file relative to the current working directory, default: '.'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :param new_simulation_name: new simulation name so the old file is not over-written, default: False (the original ``simulation_name`` is reused)
    :type new_simulation_name: bool or str
    :param bool force: if a file with the target name is already open elsewhere, open it anyway instead of auto-renaming to an available filename, default: False

.. data:: get
    :no-index:

    Extract data from an existing simulation to your Python environment.

    :param str key: name of the variable or parameter to extract. This can also be a list of fields of any combination of [``Ex``, ``Ey``, ``Ez``, ``Hx``, ``Hy``, ``Hz``, ``Sx``, ``Sy``, ``Sz``]. See :doc:`Variable Descriptions </emodeguide/variables>` for a complete list and description of all available variables. Use ``'S_matrix'`` (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only) to retrieve the scattering matrix from a solved EME chain as an :class:`SMatrix` object.
    :param str profile: label of the profile to extract the data defined by ``key`` from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: get_fields

    Extract field data from an existing simulation to your Python environment.

    :param str key: name of the field to extract a list of fields of any combination of [``Ex``, ``Ey``, ``Ez``, ``Hx``, ``Hy``, ``Hz``, ``Sx``, ``Sy``, ``Sz``].
    :type key: str or list[str]
    :param bool include_expand: whether to include the expanded region, default: True
    :param bool include_pml: whether to include the PML region, default: True
    :param bool unfold: whether to include the full window (unfolded) or strictly the solved window (potentially smaller due to applied symmetries), default: True
    :param str profile: label of the profile to extract the data defined by ``key`` from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :return: a Field object for a single-wavelength profile, or a FieldSet (a Field for each wavelength, indexable/iterable like a dict[float, Field]) for a multi-wavelength profile.
    :rtype: Field | FieldSet

.. data:: get_grid

    Extract grid data from an existing simulation to your Python environment.

    :param bool include_expand: whether to include the expanded region, default: True
    :param bool include_pml: whether to include the PML region, default: True
    :param bool unfold: whether to include the full window (unfolded) or strictly the solved window (potentially smaller due to applied symmetries), default: True
    :param str profile: label of the profile to extract the grid from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :return: a Grid object for a single-wavelength profile, or a GridSet (a Grid for each wavelength, indexable/iterable like a dict[float, Grid]) for a multi-wavelength profile.
    :rtype: Grid | GridSet

.. data:: get_shape

    Extract shape data from an existing simulation. Returns the shape object with a ``metadata`` dictionary attached (scattering and confinement results for that shape).

    :param str key: name of the shape to extract
    :param str profile: label of the profile to extract the shape from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: get_profile

    Extract a full profile object from an existing simulation. Returns a Profile object containing the settings, shapes, grid, and field data associated with the named profile.

    :param str profile: label of the profile to extract, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: create_profile_set

    Group several single-wavelength profiles into one named multi-wavelength profile set, keyed internally by wavelength. All named profiles must share identical shapes, and each must be at a distinct wavelength. The original individual profiles are deleted once grouped.

    :param profiles: names of the profiles to group
    :type profiles: str or list[str]
    :param str profile_set_name: name of the resulting profile set, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: delete_profile

    Delete a named profile (or reset the ``_default`` profile's settings) from the simulation file.

    :param str profile: name of the profile to delete
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: clear_field_data

    Deletes the following data from every profile to reduce the '.eph' file size: ``Fx``, ``Fy``, ``Ex``, ``Ey``, ``Ez``, ``Hx``, ``Hy``, ``Hz``, ``Sx``, ``Sy``, ``Sz``, ``x``, ``y``, ``permittivity``, ``permeability``.

    :param str profile: currently ignored; field data is cleared from all profiles regardless of this argument, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: save

    Saves a simulation file and keeps the simulation file in the 'open' state.

    :param bool save_all_fields: whether all field data should be saved (so the ``E``, ``H``, and ``S`` fields can be accessed without an EMode license) or just the raw field data (``Fx`` and ``Fy``), default: False
    :param str file_type: file type to save the simulation file as, either 'eph' or 'mat', default: 'eph'
    :param bool close: whether to close the simulation file after saving, default: False
    :param str new_save_path: if set, saves the simulation file in this new path, default: None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: close

    Saves or deletes a simulation file. This function is called through the "close" method of emodeconnection, and these optional parameters can be passed directly to the "close" method.

    :param bool save: saves simulation file if True and deletes the simulation file if False, default: True
    :param bool save_all_fields: whether all field data should be saved (so the ``E``, ``H``, and ``S`` fields can be accessed without an EMode license) or just the raw field data (``Fx`` and ``Fy``), default: False
    :param str file_type: file type to save the simulation file as, either 'eph' or 'mat', default: 'eph'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'



EME
---

Every section function below accepts a ``ports`` argument, which names, windows, or displaces the ports on either end of the section, in place of its default left and right ports. Sections are otherwise connected in the order they are declared; use :data:`connect_ports` to wire named ports explicitly instead, including into branching topologies. See :ref:`ports` for the port model and the ``Port`` and ``Bounds`` classes.

.. data:: EME_settings

    Declare global EME defaults that are inherited by sections created afterward. Each parameter left unspecified leaves the corresponding stored default unchanged. A section's own ``settings`` argument at creation still overrides these globals. Sections created before this call are not affected.

    :param apply_scattering: whether interfacial scattering loss is automatically applied to the S-matrix, either for every wavelength (True), no wavelengths (False), or only the listed wavelengths, default: False
    :type apply_scattering: bool or list[float]
    :param str beta_interpolation: either 'uniform' or 'linear' to specify how the propagation constant is interpolated between z-slices of a taper/gds section, default: 'uniform'
    :param junction_normalization: controls how junction S-matrices are power-normalized; either a single bool/'gain' value applied to both junction kinds, or a dict with 'inter_section' and 'intra_section' keys, each accepting True (full SVD unitarization), False (raw, unnormalized), or 'gain' (clip singular values at 1 while keeping the raw lossy mode-matching), default: 'gain' for inter-section junctions and True for intra-section junctions
    :type junction_normalization: bool or str or dict
    :param float overlap_variation: threshold of mode-list overlap between z-slices used by the automatic z-slicing bisection for taper/gds sections, default: 0.01
    :param float minimum_z_step: [nm] the minimum allowed z-step for the automatic z-slicing bisection, default: 0.1
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: straight_section

    Define a uniform-cross-section waveguide section for the EME solver. Sections are placed sequentially in the z-direction in the order they are declared (or updated, if ``name`` already exists).

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: label of the profile that defines the section's cross-section
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
    :param offset: [nm] transverse displacement of this section relative to whatever its ports connect to; if only a single value is given it is assumed to be the x-offset, default: (0, 0). **Legacy**: this is the same displacement as :class:`Port`'s own ``offset`` applied to every port of the section at once, and setting both on one section raises an error. Prefer declaring ``offset`` on the specific port that sits off-axis.
    :type offset: float or tuple[float, float]
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, merged onto the current global EME settings (or onto the section's existing settings, when updating), default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: pwd_section

    Define a free space section, in which the field is expanded in plane waves (a plane-wave decomposition, PWD) over a uniform material, rather than in the guided modes of a cross-section. This is intended for gaps, facets, and free space propagation between waveguide sections; the junctions between a free space section and its neighbors are computed analytically instead of from a mode solve.

    The basis is the set of plane-wave harmonics of the section window, with transverse wavevectors ``kx = 2*pi*m/window_width`` and ``ky = 2*pi*n/window_height``, each harmonic carrying both a TE and a TM polarization. At least one of ``max_order``, ``max_kt``, or ``num_modes`` is required to truncate the basis; when more than one is given, they are applied in the order ``max_order``, ``max_kt``, ``num_modes``.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
    :param material: the material filling the section, either a material name (from the material database) or a ~MaterialProperties or ~MaterialSpec object; must be isotropic, default: "Vacuum"
    :type material: str or ~MaterialProperties or ~MaterialSpec
    :param str profile: label of the profile that supplies the default window and the wavelength(s) of the section, default: '_default'
    :param window: [nm] the (width, height) of the plane-wave window, which overrides the window of ``profile``, default: None (use the ``window_width`` and ``window_height`` of ``profile``)
    :type window: tuple[float, float] or None
    :param offset: [nm] transverse displacement of the window's origin, which is its horizontal center and bottom edge, default: (0, 0)
    :type offset: tuple[float, float]
    :param max_order: the largest harmonic order to keep in the x- and y-directions, so that ``|m| <= max_order[0]`` and ``|n| <= max_order[1]``, default: None
    :type max_order: tuple[int, int] or None
    :param float max_kt: [1/nm] the largest transverse wavevector magnitude to keep, default: None
    :param int num_modes: the largest number of modes to keep, counting both polarizations of each harmonic, and applied after ``max_order`` and ``max_kt``; the basis always keeps a harmonic together with its opposite-direction pair, so the resulting count can land slightly below the requested value, default: None
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: taper_section

    Define a section that linearly interpolates its cross-section between two profiles for the EME solver, automatically slicing the z-direction to track the mode evolution.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: label of the profile that defines the section beginning
    :param str profile_end: label of the profile that defines the section ending
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings` (notably ``overlap_variation`` and ``minimum_z_step``, which control the automatic z-slicing), default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: gds_section

    Define a section whose cross-section varies along z according to a mask imported from a GDS file, for more complex geometries defined with third-party layout tools.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: label of the profile that defines the section's cross-section outside of the GDS mask
    :param str gds_path: path to the GDS file used to mask the section
    :param layer_map: mapping of profile shape names to GDS layer numbers, used to determine which shapes in ``profile`` are masked by which GDS layer
    :type layer_map: dict[str, int]
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section, default: derived from the GDS bounding box
    :param cell_index: the cell index (or name) in the specified GDS file, default: 0
    :type cell_index: int or str
    :param float scale: unit scale factor applied to the GDS coordinates (e.g. use 1000 if the GDS file is drawn in microns but the simulation is in nanometers), default: 1
    :param port_poses: explicit port positions/orientations at the section boundaries, default: derived from the GDS bounding box (left port at w=0, right port at w=length)
    :type port_poses: dict
    :param bool heal: whether to heal small gaps/self-intersections in the imported GDS polygons before meshing, default: True
    :param float grow: amount to grow imported GDS polygons by, to close small gaps, default: 1e-3
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. note::
    Once sections are declared, call ``plot()`` with ``plane='z-x'`` or ``plane='z-y'`` to preview a geometry-only 'Outline' of the section layout before running :data:`EME`.

..
    .. data:: TO_section

        Define a section whose geometry is generated analytically via a transformation-optics (TO) coordinate transform, rather than from a fixed cross-section or an imported GDS mask. This is a beta feature.

        :param str name: section name
        :param str transform: either 'coupler' (a two-waveguide directional coupler) or 'parameterized_curve' (a single waveguide with arbitrary bending)
        :param str profile: label of the profile that defines the waveguide cross-section
        :param waveguides: the :class:`~emodeconnection.geometry.Path` centerline(s) of the waveguide(s); 'coupler' requires exactly 2, 'parameterized_curve' requires exactly 1
        :type waveguides: list
        :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
        :param poses: the :class:`~emodeconnection.geometry.Pose` of each waveguide's local frame within the section frame; required (length 2) for 'coupler', ignored for 'parameterized_curve'
        :type poses: list
        :param float width: the lateral extent of the transform region; required for 'coupler', ignored for 'parameterized_curve'
        :param float virtual_gap: extra lateral padding used internally by the coupler transform to avoid a coordinate singularity; required for 'coupler', ignored for 'parameterized_curve'
        :param center_path: an optional additional :class:`~emodeconnection.geometry.Path` defining the coupler's central symmetry curve; only used for 'coupler', default: None
        :param int theta_grid_points: number of grid points used to sample the transform's angular coordinate; only used for 'parameterized_curve', default: 2001
        :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
        :type settings: dict or None
        :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

        .. note::
            Once created, a ``TO_section`` can only be updated through ``TO_section`` itself; its geometry cannot be reshaped through :data:`straight_section`/:data:`taper_section`/:data:`gds_section`.

    .. data:: to_gds

        Export a previously declared 'coupler' :data:`TO_section` to a GDS file, for fabrication preview and to inspect the geometry that the EME solver will build.

        :param str name: name of the ``TO_section`` (transform 'coupler') to export
        :param str path: file path to write the GDS library to
        :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: copy_section

    Place a second instance of an already-declared section in the chain, reusing its already-computed S-matrix instead of re-solving it.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str section_name: name of the existing section to copy
    :param bool mirror: whether to reverse the placement along the propagation direction (swapping the left/right ports), default: False
    :param port_swap: explicit port-name mapping to use instead of the automatically computed left/right swap when ``mirror`` is True, default: None
    :type port_swap: dict
    :param ports: relabel/window this copy's own left/right boundary, with the same semantics as any other section's ``ports``, independent of ``port_swap`` and of the source section's own ports. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: connect_ports

    Override the default left/right adjacency wiring between named ports declared with the ``ports`` argument of any section function.

    Connecting two ports also **pins their coordinate systems together**: the two ports' origins (the horizontal centre and bottom edge of each cross-section) are made to coincide, so the connection is what positions one section relative to the other. Use :class:`Port`'s ``offset`` to displace a section off that shared origin, and its ``window`` to choose which part of a wider cross-section the port exposes. The first section you declare defines the global frame that plots are drawn in.

    :param pairs: a list of ``('<section_name>.<port_name>', '<section_name>.<port_name>')`` pairs to connect, e.g. ``[('a.right', 'b.left'), ('c.right', 'd.left')]``. A port can only have one connection, so declaring a new connection for a port that already had one supersedes it. Names are resolved against the actual declared sections/ports at :data:`EME` build time.
    :type pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: EME

    Calculate the complete scattering matrix of all defined sections using the eigenmode expansion method (EME).

    :param bool warm_start: whether to seed each taper/gds section's automatic z-slice refinement from the previously solved chain (when available), instead of re-refining from scratch, default: False
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: plot_S_matrix

    Colormap plot of the transmission or reflection component of the EME scattering matrix.

    :param input: input field (first number of the scattering matrix identifier), default: 0
    :type input: int or str
    :param output: output field (second number of the scattering matrix identifier), default: 1
    :type output: int or str
    :param plot_function: specify the function to apply to the plot data ('abs^2', 'angle', 'real', 'imag'), default: 'abs^2'
    :type plot_function: str or None
    :param str file_name: if specified, forces the function to save a file with the given parameters and will not display the interactive plot, file is saved under a directory called EM_figures, default: None
    :param str file_type: file type for saving a plot, ‘pdf’ or ‘png’, default: '' (no extension is added to ``file_name`` unless a file type is given)
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'



Multi-Physics
-------------

.. data:: heat

    Run a steady-state thermal simulation of a waveguide cross-section. Requires a '3D' license.

    .. warning::
        This function is only available under beta release. Please report any issues or bugs.

    .. note::
        Each ``shape()`` now accepts an input parameter called ``heat_only`` (default: False), which can be used to set additional shapes on top or bottom of the photonic layer stack. For example, common ``heat_only`` shapes are the substrate and metal heater layers.

        Each ``shape()`` also now accepts an input parameter called ``fem_resolution`` (default: 500), which is used to refine the triangular mesh within certain shapes.

        Each material in the EMode material database now has ``thermal_conductivity`` (W/m·K), ``resistivity`` (Ohm·nm), and ``dn_dT`` (1/K).

    :param float min_angle: Minimum angle for triangular mesh. Smaller values result in a finer mesh, but can prevent the meshing algorithm from converging. Default: 30.
    :param float boundary_temperature: Fixed temperature boundary condition in 'K' set along each perimeter indicated by ``boundaries``. Default: 298.
    :param list[str] boundaries:  'top', 'bottom', 'left', or 'right'; Indicates which boundaries are set to the fixed temperature ``boundary_temperature``. Default: ['bottom'].
    :param bool verbose: Control the display of the progress bar. Default: True.
    :param str simulation_name: Simulation name. Default: 'emode'.
    :return: A dictionary/struct with the mesh points (``p``), mesh triangles (``t``), ``temperature``, ``thermal_conductivity``, and ``heat_generation`` arrays. It also includes the ``boundary_temperature`` and ``boundaries`` settings.

.. data:: electrostatic

    Run a steady-state electrostatic simulation of a waveguide cross-section. Requires a '3D' license.

    .. warning::
        This function is only available under beta release. Please report any issues or bugs.

    .. note::
        Each ``shape()`` also now accepts an input parameter called ``voltage`` (default: None), which is set to create electric field sources. Shapes with ``voltage`` left as None do not get a voltage boundary condition applied.

        Each ``shape()`` also now accepts an input parameter called ``fem_resolution`` (default: 500), which is used to refine the triangular mesh within certain shapes.

        Each material in the EMode material database now has ``eps_r_dc`` (relative permittivity at ~1 kHz).

    :param float min_angle: Minimum angle for triangular mesh. Smaller values result in a finer mesh, but can prevent the meshing algorithm from converging. Default: 30.
    :param bool verbose: Control the display of the progress bar. Default: True.
    :param str simulation_name: Simulation name. Default: 'emode'.
    :return: A dictionary/struct with the mesh points (``p``), mesh triangles (``t``), ``voltage``, and ``eps_dc_grid``.



Material Database
-----------------

Descriptions of all materials available in built-in material database. This information is also accessible from ``refractive_index`` and ``material_explorer``. Unless specified otherwise, all materials have :math:`\mu = 1.0`. Each equation for the refractive index assumes that the wavelength :math:`\lambda` has units of :math:`\mu\mathrm{m}`.

.. data:: Air
    
    .. math:: n = \left(1 + \frac{5.79211 \times 10^{-2}}{238.019 - \lambda^{-2}} + \frac{1.67917 \times 10^{-3}}{57.3620 - \lambda^{-2}}\right)
    
    Wavelength range: 200 nm to 2000 nm
    
        | P. E. Ciddor, "Refractive index of air: new equations for the visible and near infrared," Appl. Opt. 35, 1566 (1996).

.. data:: AlGaAs
    
    .. math::
        
        \mathrm{Al}_x &\mathrm{Ga}_{1-x}\mathrm{As} \\\ \\
        E_0 &= 3.65 + 0.871 x + 0.179 x^2 \\
        E_\mathrm{d} &= 36.1 - 2.45 x \\
        E_\Gamma &= 1.424 + 1.266 x + 0.26 x^2 \\
        E_\mathrm{f} &= (2 E_0^2 - E_\Gamma^2)^{0.5} \\
        \eta &= \pi E_\mathrm{d}/(2 E_0^3 (E_0^2 - E_\Gamma^2)) \\
        M_1 &= \frac{\eta}{2 \pi} (E_\mathrm{f}^4 - E_\Gamma^4) \\
        M_3 &= \frac{\eta}{\pi} (E_\mathrm{f}^2 - E_\Gamma^2) \\
        E &= h c/ \lambda ,\\
        &\mathrm{where}\:h\:\mathrm{is\:Planck's\:constant\:and}\:c\:\mathrm{is\:the\:speed\:of\:light\:in\:vacuum.} \\
        \chi &= M_1 + M_3 E^2 + \frac{\eta}{\pi} E^4 \mathrm{ln}((E_\mathrm{f}^2 - E^2)/(2 E_\Gamma - E^2)) \\
        n &= (\chi + 1)^{0.5} \\
        
    
    Wavelength range: 689 nm to 1033 nm
    
        | M. A. Afromowitz, "Refractive index of Ga_{1-x}Al_{x}As," Solid State Commun. 15, 59 (1974).
        | Notes: requires Al fraction input (x between 0 and 1), which defaults to x=1: "AlGaAs, x".

.. data:: AlN
